questions.q: What does the summary say about the world women live in?
a: It was designed around men's bodies and needs
It has achieved equality in most public spaces
It favors women in health and safety testing
It was rebuilt after women entered the workforce
questions.why: Lesson 1 concludes that cities and infrastructure were designed for men, making life harder for women.

questions.q: What example shows that car safety testing favors men?
a: Cars are tested on male bodies, so women are hurt more
Cars use seatbelts designed only for children
Crash tests are only required in a few countries
Women are less likely to wear seatbelts
questions.why: Lesson 2 says testing is not required on female models, and women suffer more severe injuries.

questions.q: What problem does the summary point out about office temperatures?
a: They were set using an average 40-year-old man
They are kept too warm for most employees
They change too often during the workday
They are controlled by individual workers
questions.why: Lesson 2 says air conditioning standards from the 1960s were based on a male body.

questions.q: How many seats in national legislatures do women hold worldwide?
a: About 20 percent
About 30 percent
About 40 percent
About 50 percent
questions.why: Lesson 3 says women hold only about a fifth of seats, despite being half the population.

questions.q: What does the summary say happens when women speak up in finance or politics?
a: They are judged more harshly than men saying the same thing
They are praised for bringing a fresh perspective
They are given more speaking time than men
They are usually ignored by the audience
questions.why: Lesson 3 says identical statements earn women negative perceptions while men appear knowledgeable.
